thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: page fired → service=private-controlplane-vpc customer=acme-corp severity=high

pagerduty-bot: PD Alert PD12345: control-plane heartbeats missing for customer-vpc acme-prod (3/3 control-plane nodes). Auto-escalation in 5m if not acked.

sara (oncall): acked — I'm joining. @jamal can you pull the control plane metrics?

jamal (eng): looking. I'm seeing heartbeat drop starting ~00:05 UTC, RTT to customer VPC control plane jumps, control-plane API 502s.

liam (sre): seeing similar on infra side: BGP sessions to acme edge changed state, route flap visible in edge-router logs.

olivia (support): Maria from CS just DMed — their app saw 503s and retries. They're actively impacted.

maria (cs): yes customer reports 40% failed requests, intermittent reconnects. They've paused non-critical traffic.

kevin (infra): pulling router logs for acme-cust vpc now. Could be a peering egress issue to the private control plane.

jamal (eng): running runbook step 1: verify control plane pods healthy on our side. `kubectl -n controlplane get pods -o wide` shows controller-manager stuck restarting on node gpux-07.

liam (sre): gpux-07 had a kernel panic flash earlier in the hour, kubelet still restarted but network plug-in reports flaps. Could be NIC firmware.

sara (oncall): immediate mitigation: 1) move acme's control plane traffic to warm standby region; 2) ask support to throttle customer traffic? are we able to do quick failover?

kevin (infra): we can bump routing policy to prefer standby region; prepping a controlled reroute. Will need a 60s window to update BGP communities.

jamal (eng): prepare canary failover config. I'll stage the control-plane instance in standby, ensure certs are valid.

olivia (support): telling acme CS to expect ~5-10m maintenance; they'll give customer the heads up. Maria, can you confirm any scheduled maintenance on their side?

maria (cs): none. They're surprised. Providing their incident lead contact now.

incident-bot: PagerDuty PD12345 — acknowledged by sara (oncall) at 1749987675. Escalation paused.

liam (sre): Proposed short-term action: rehome control-plane pods away from gpux-07 and re-provision that node; long-term: NIC firmware roll for gpux cohort.

jamal (eng): quick command to evacuate: `kubectl drain gpux-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then `kubectl apply -f acme-controlplane-standby.yaml` (standby has hot certs).

kevin (infra): BGP prep done. On my mark I will push community change to prefer standby: `netops update-route acme-prod prefer-standby`. Will push at :45s.

sara (oncall): do it. jamal, kevin, liam — coordinate. I'll sit in the bridge and narrate for CS and customer.

jamal (eng): draining now. Pods terminating, IPs reallocated.

kevin (infra): pushing route change... done. Please monitor.

liam (sre): node gpux-07 drained successfully. Control-plane instances in standby are taking leader leases. API healthy on standby.

olivia (support): messaging sent to acme contact: "We've rerouted control-plane traffic to standby region to mitigate packet loss; services should stabilize. We'll follow up with RCA."

maria (cs): customer confirms retries dropping and 200s returning. They're bringing traffic back gradually.

sara (oncall): acknowledged. I'll keep the incident open until we replace gpux-07 and observe 30m of stable control-plane health. Next steps: schedule node reprovision, firmware patch window, postmortem owner jamal.

jamal (eng): taking postmortem. I'll collect kubelet, kernel logs, and BGP dump.

liam (sre): I'll queue gpux-07 for reprovision and NIC firmware update after postmortem.

incident-bot: PagerDuty PD12345 — status: mitigated (failover to standby). SLA impact: partial for acme-corp (approx 8 minutes).

sara (oncall): thanks all. I'll handoff to jamal for RCA and liam for infra follow-up. Closing watch in 30m unless regressions. :thumbsup:

jamal (eng): noted — will file RCA and follow-up action items.

kevin (infra): adding firmware rollout to infra maintenance backlog.

olivia (support): closing the loop with acme. They asked for postmortem; will coordinate delivery with jamal and maria.

maria (cs): thanks team — customer appreciative of the fast mitigation.

sara (oncall): handing off to next oncall (liam) at 1749987900 — please monitor for 30m, escalate back if anything spikes.
